releases.name: PlexusOne Desktop v0.7.0
releases.body:
# v0.7.0

**Release Date:** 2026-10-29

## Highlights

- **Claude names everywhere** - Pane headers and the Claude Sessions window show each session's Claude name, such as `github-com-8b`, and its live status
- **Know when a session needs you** - A notification, a Dock badge, and `⌘J` take you to sessions waiting at a permission prompt or other question
- **Crash recovery in one step** - Restoring saved windows recreates missing tmux sessions by resuming the Claude session that ran in each, and an optional hook remembers tmux names while the app is closed

## What's New

### Claude Names and Live Status

Claude Code names each session, and sessions use these names to address each other, while you know panes by their tmux name. PlexusOne Desktop now shows both:

- Each pane header shows the Claude name after the tmux session name. When the session is waiting for you, an orange badge says what for, such as `waiting: permission prompt`.
- The Claude Sessions window has a **Claude Name** column, shows a running session's live status (`busy`, `idle`, or what it is waiting for) beside its state, and searches by name.
- The app keeps a tmux option, `@claude_name`, on each tmux session, so your tmux status line can show the name too. Add these lines to `~/.tmux.conf`:

```tmux
set -g status-left '[#S]#{?@claude_name,[#{@claude_name}],} '
set -g status-left-length 40
```

### Waiting Sessions

- When a Claude session starts waiting for you, PlexusOne Desktop posts a notification such as *"github-com-8b in tmux acad is waiting: permission prompt"*. Click it to go to that session. Turn notifications off in **Settings > Sessions**.
- The Dock icon shows how many sessions are waiting.
- **Window > Jump to Next Waiting Session** (`⌘J`) cycles through them.
- Going to a session focuses the pane already showing it, in whichever window it is, and opens a window only when no pane shows it. Double-clicking a running session in the Claude Sessions window does the same.

### More in the Claude Sessions Window

- **Last Prompt** and **Cost** columns; the detail pane also shows lines added and removed, from Claude Code's cost record.
- The **Repository** column shows where a session did its work, ranked by how many of the files it read or edited fall in each repository, rather than the directory it started in.
- **Rename Claude Session...** (right-click a running session) types `/rename <name>` into the session's pane. It is available only while the session is idle at its prompt, so it cannot interrupt work.

### Crash Recovery

- **Restore at launch recreates tmux sessions.** When the saved windows expect tmux sessions that no longer exist, each is recreated under the same name by resuming the Claude session that last ran in it. The windows then open with their saved layouts.
- **Optional Claude Code hook.** By itself the app learns a session's tmux name only while it runs. **Settings > Sessions > Install Hook** adds two Claude Code hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json` (backed up first; only the app's own entries are touched). Each Claude session then records its tmux pane at start and on every prompt, even while PlexusOne Desktop is closed. **Remove Hook** takes them out again.

See the [Claude Sessions guide](https://github.com/plexusone/plexusone-app/blob/main/docs/guides/desktop/claude-sessions.md).

## What's Changed

- Only one copy of PlexusOne Desktop runs at a time. Opening a second copy brings the running one forward, so two copies never write the same state files.
- When Claude Code's live record lacks a tmux location, the app finds the session's pane from the process tree.

## What's Fixed

- TUI Parser handles errors from HTTP writes, PTY and server closes, detaching, and sending keys instead of ignoring them.

## Documentation

- The Claude Sessions guide covers Claude names, the tmux status line, waiting alerts, renaming, the hook, and crash recovery
- [ADR 0003](https://github.com/plexusone/plexusone-app/blob/main/docs/design/adrs/0003-claude-code-hook-recording.md): recording sessions with a Claude Code hook
- Building requires Xcode 16 or later, since SwiftTerm 1.20 needs Swift tools 6.0; the guides now say so
- The configuration reference lists the Claude session files and the tmux status line for Claude names
- Agent guidance moved from `CLAUDE.md` to `AGENTS.md`, which `CLAUDE.md` imports

## Upgrading

Quit the running PlexusOne Desktop before opening the new version. With only one copy allowed to run, opening v0.7.0 while v0.6.0 is running brings v0.6.0 forward instead.

## Install

Open the `.dmg` and drag PlexusOne Desktop to Applications. Builds are ad-hoc signed but not notarized: on first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

| macOS Universal | [PlexusOneDesktop-0.7.0-macos-universal.dmg](https://github.com/plexusone/plexusone-app/releases/download/v0.7.0/PlexusOneDesktop-0.7.0-macos-universal.dmg) |

releases.name: PlexusOne Desktop v0.6.0
releases.body:
# v0.6.0

**Release Date:** 2026-10-27

## Highlights

- **Claude Sessions window** - See every Claude Code session with its tmux session, subject, repositories, last activity, and how it ended, and bring back the ones you want after a crash or restart
- **Trackpad scrolls the conversation** - Scrolling now moves back through a session's history instead of stepping through Claude Code's past prompts
- **Menus and multiple windows work** - New Session, Attach, Detach, and Next/Previous Pane act on the front window, and restoring several saved windows no longer hangs

## What's New

### Claude Sessions Window

Open it with **File > Claude Sessions...** (`⇧⌘S`) or the list button in a window's toolbar.

Each Claude Code session shows its tmux session, its subject (Claude's title, else the first prompt), the git repositories it worked in as `github.com/org/repo`, when it was last active, and its session ID. Select a session for its full details: directory, branch, first and last prompts, every repository it read or edited, and the command that resumes it. Filter by how recently a session was active, by state, or by search.

The window also shows how each session ended:

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Running | Claude Code is running |
| Exited normally | Claude exited while its tmux pane stayed open, for example with `/exit` or Ctrl+C |
| tmux/terminal closed | The tmux pane, session, or server closed while Claude was running in it |
| System shutdown | Claude was still running when the machine shut down, restarted, or crashed |
| Crashed/killed | The Claude process died without cleaning up |
| Ended cleanly | Claude shut down cleanly while PlexusOne Desktop was not running |
| Ended abnormally | No clean shutdown was recorded and the machine has not restarted since |

Claude Code's own files show whether it shut down cleanly, but a closed terminal looks the same as `/exit` there. PlexusOne Desktop tells them apart by watching while it runs, and it remembers each session's tmux name in `~/.plexusone/claude-sessions.json`.

**Restoring sessions:** double-click a session, or select several and choose Resume. For each session you choose the tmux session name; the remembered name is filled in when there is one. PlexusOne types `claude --resume <id>` into a new shell in the session's directory, in a new window of that tmux session if it still exists, or in a new tmux session. The restored sessions open together in one window. After a crash, a banner offers to restore every session that ended abnormally in the last 48 hours.

See the [Claude Sessions guide](https://github.com/plexusone/plexusone-app/blob/main/docs/guides/desktop/claude-sessions.md).

### Keyboard Commands

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⇧⌘S` | Claude Sessions window |
| `⌥⌘A` | Attach a session to the focused pane |
| `⇧⌘A` | Detach the focused pane |
| `⌘]` / `⌘[` | Next / previous pane |

Attach moved from `⌘A`, which is Select All again.

## What's Fixed

### Trackpad Scrolling

With tmux mouse mode off, tmux keeps the terminal on its alternate screen, where scrolling is sent as Up/Down keys. In Claude Code those keys step through past prompts, so the trackpad could not scroll back through a conversation. Attaching a pane now turns on tmux mouse mode for that tmux session only, so scrolling moves through its history. Up/Down still navigate prompt history, and holding Shift while dragging selects text as before. Your `~/.tmux.conf` is not changed; to keep your own tmux mouse setting, turn off **Settings > Sessions > Trackpad scrolls conversation history**.

### Windows and Menus

- Restoring two or more saved windows hung the app; each additional window now opens with its saved layout
- New Window and Pop Out opened one window for every window already open
- New Session, Attach, Detach, and Next/Previous Pane did nothing; they now act on the front window

### Panes

- Pane headers and the status bar show each session's current status instead of its status when the pane was attached
- The input-needed badge clears once the prompt is answered, and notifications fire once when a prompt appears rather than on every redraw
- Scrolling works on an unfocused pane, and typing scrolls a pane back to its latest output
- Switching or detaching a pane no longer leaves a zombie tmux process

### Sessions

- Session list updates run on the main thread, and tmux commands no longer block threads Swift's concurrency runtime depends on
- tmux session names containing `|` are listed correctly, and blank names are rejected

## Dependencies

- SwiftTerm 1.20.0 (from 1.19.0) for the desktop and iOS apps. SwiftTerm 1.99 requires Xcode 26 and stays out until CI builds with it.

## Infrastructure

- The GitHub release page now shows these release notes, followed by the generated list of changes

## Documentation

- Claude Sessions guide and updated keyboard shortcuts
- Maintainers guide with the release process, including a trial run of the release build before tagging
- Docs reorganized into `docs/guides/`, `docs/design/` (architecture and decision records), `docs/specs/`, and `docs/releases/`
- Architecture decision records for session end detection and tmux mouse mode

## Install

Open the `.dmg` and drag PlexusOne Desktop to Applications. Builds are ad-hoc signed but not notarized: on first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

releases.name: v0.2.0
releases.body:
# Release Notes - v0.2.0

**Release Date:** 2026-10-05

## Overview

Adds the Agent/Team Definition Registry: a persistent, queryable inventory of the agents and teams discovered across registered repos, replacing the stateless, read-on-every-request behavior of the visual designer with stable identity and drift detection.

## Highlights

- **Agent/Team Definition Registry** - Agents and teams discovered in `specs/agents/*.md` and `specs/teams/*.json` across registered repos are upserted into persistent `AgentDefinition` and `TeamDefinition` records, keyed by `(repo, namespace, name)` so identity survives file moves
- **Dangling-reference detection** - Every sync validates a team's roster, orchestrator, and agent-assigned workflow steps against what's actually registered, via `multi-agent-spec`'s `Team.ValidateAgentReferences`
- **Always current** - Registration runs at startup, re-runs automatically on spec file changes, and can be triggered on demand

## Features

### Registry

- **Stable identity** - Each `AgentDefinition`/`TeamDefinition` carries a `registry_xrn` and a `source_ref` derived from the owning repo's module path, independent of file location
- **Content-hash drift detection** - Re-syncing unchanged files only refreshes `last_seen_at`; changed files update the record and increment the sync result's counters
- **Team membership resolution** - Teams resolve their roster to registered agent IDs via an ent M2M edge, refreshed on every sync (not just when the team file changes) so an agent registered after its team references it still gets linked
- **Resilient sync** - A malformed agent spec file produces a warning rather than aborting registration for the rest of the repo or workspace
- **Concurrency-safe** - Watcher-triggered and HTTP-triggered syncs are serialized behind a mutex so they can't race on the same unique-index insert

### API

- `GET /api/registry/agents` - List registered agent definitions
- `GET /api/registry/teams` - List registered team definitions with resolved members
- `POST /api/registry/sync` - Re-scan all spec directories and upsert the registry on demand

## Getting Started

```bash
# Build
make build

# Run with workspace - registration happens automatically at startup
./specui --workspace ~/path/to/agentplexus

# Query the registry
curl http://localhost:8090/api/registry/agents
curl http://localhost:8090/api/registry/teams
```

## Known Limitations

- Repos without a `multi-agent-spec` `specs/` directory (e.g. hosted, non-interactive agent systems) aren't registered yet
- No marketplace, evaluation/rubric tracking, or cost/telemetry - this release is the Definition plane only

## Contributors

- John Wang (@grokify)
- Claude Sonnet 5 (AI pair programmer)

releases.name: v0.1.0
releases.body:
# Release Notes - v0.1.0

**Release Date:** 2026-01-25

## Overview

Initial release of Multi-Agent Designer, a visual workflow designer for exploring and managing multi-agent team specifications.

## Highlights

- **Visual Workflow Designer** - React Flow canvas for visualizing agent teams with custom nodes showing agent icons and model-based coloring
- **Gmail-Style Floating Panels** - View agent details in draggable, resizable, minimizable panels that can be positioned anywhere on screen
- **Persistent Views** - Save and restore your UI layouts including selected teams, node positions, and sidebar width using SQLite or PostgreSQL

## Features

### Frontend

- **React Flow Canvas**
  - Interactive drag-and-drop agent nodes
  - Automatic edge layout showing agent dependencies
  - Custom node styling with model-based colors (opus=red, sonnet=blue, haiku=green)
  - Support for agent icons (react, go, postgresql, etc.)

- **Floating Panels**
  - Open multiple agent detail panels simultaneously
  - Drag panels anywhere on screen
  - Resize from top-left or bottom-right corners
  - Minimize to header bar
  - Panel headers colored to match agent model
  - Staggered positioning for new panels

- **Multi-Team View**
  - Display up to 4 teams in a 2x2 grid layout
  - Each team canvas is independent with its own zoom/pan
  - Team labels in top-left corner

- **Views Management**
  - Save current layout as a named view
  - Load saved views from dropdown
  - Update existing views with current layout
  - Delete views no longer needed

- **Agent Details**
  - Model and namespace metadata
  - Description text
  - Tools and dependencies badges
  - Instructions with HTML/Code toggle
  - Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting

### Backend

- **HTTP Server**
  - Embedded frontend assets
  - RESTful API for teams, agents, and views
  - Graceful shutdown

- **File Watcher**
  - Monitors spec directories for changes
  - Automatically reloads team data
  - No server restart required

- **Database**
  - Ent ORM with auto-migration
  - SQLite for local development (default)
  - PostgreSQL for production deployments
  - Environment-based configuration

## Getting Started

```bash
# Build
make build

# Run with workspace
./specui --workspace ~/path/to/agentplexus

# Open browser
open http://localhost:8090
```

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `DB_DRIVER` | `sqlite` | Database driver |
| `DB_DSN` | `file:data/specui.db?_pragma=foreign_keys(1)` | Connection string |

## Known Limitations

- Maximum 4 teams displayed simultaneously
- Panel positions not persisted in views (only node positions)
- No search/filter functionality yet

## Contributors

- John Wang (@grokify)
- Claude Opus 4.5 (AI pair programmer)
